content.title: Liverpool vs PSG Lineups, Injuries, Live Streaming, Cable, How & Where to Watch
content.text: Liverpool host Paris Saint-Germain at Anfield as the Reds look to overcome a 2-0 deficit to secure their place in the Champions League semi-final.Arne Slot’s side enters the match following an encouraging domestic victory over Fulham. Goals from Rio Ngumoha and Mohamed Salah in that fixture ensured the club remained in fifth place in the Premier League standings.Despite the pressure, Slot has expressed full confidence in his squad, maintaining that the team is capable of delivering a historic performance in front of their home supporters."Yes, there is a belief we can do special things but we also need to be very, very, very special because we are playing against the champions of Europe, so that makes the task more complicated but not impossible," he said.Arne Slot, Manager of Liverpool, looks on prior to the Premier League match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Liverpool.Photo by David Rogers/Getty ImagesMeanwhile, PSG have had a period of rest, having not played a competitive fixture since the opening leg. Historical records might also favor the visitors. Liverpool have progressed only twice, in 1991 and 2019, when trying to overturn a deficit of two goals or more after losing the first leg away from home.Liverpool vs PSG Official Lineups and InjuriesLiverpool remains without the services of Alisson Becker, Wataru Endo, Giovanni Leoni, and Conor Bradley. However, Curtis Jones is expected to be available for selection despite an injury scare against Fulham.As for Paris Saint-Germain, Fabian Ruiz is ruled out with a knee injury, but Bradley Barcola could make his return to the squad after recovering from an ankle issue.Liverpool:Goalkeeper: MamardashviliDefenders: Frimpong, Konaté, Van Dijk, KerkezMidfielders: Gravenberch, Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, WirtzForwards: Isak, EkitikePSG:Goalkeeper: SafonovDefenders: Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, N. MendesMidfielders: Vitinha, J. Neves, Zaïre-EmeryForward: Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé, DouéHow and Where to Watch Liverpool vs PSGThe Liverpool vs. PSG UEFA Champions League quarterfinal second leg will kick off at 3:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, April 14, 2026.US viewers can watch it live on Paramount+, with coverage also available for Spanish fans on ViX, UNIMÁS, or TUDN.This story was originally published by Athlon Sports on Apr 14, 2026, where it first appeared in the Soccer section. Add Athlon Sports as a Preferred Source by clicking here.PSG and Luis Enrique sweat on Vitinha ahead of Champions League semisTue, April 21, 2026 at 7:31 AM CDTVitinha (R) will miss Paris Saint-Germain's Ligue 1 clash against Nantes due to a heel inflammation (Paul ELLIS) (Paul ELLIS/AFP/AFP)Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique said Tuesday he was unsure if midfield metronome Vitinha would be fit to play against Bayern Munich in the Champions League semi-finals.The Portuguese central midfielder will miss PSG's Ligue 1 clash against Nantes on Wednesday due to a heel inflammation."We'll take a calm and measured approach to see how the injured players can make a comeback. But I don't know," he told reporters when asked if Vitinha would be back in time for next Tuesday's semi-final first leg at the Parc des Princes."We need to manage Vitinha's minor injury; some players are a bit tired or have a few niggles," the Spaniard also told PSGTV.Should the 26-year-old be unavailable, his place at the heart of the PSG midfield could be filled by the returning Fabian Ruiz.Alongside Vitinha and Joao Neves, Ruiz formed the midfield trio that anchored much of PSG's success last season as they won a maiden Champions League title and lifted the Ligue 1 trophy.The Spaniard returned for the final 18 minutes of PSG's 2-1 league loss at home to Lyon last weekend as he continues his comeback from a knee injury.Luis Enrique cooled expectations on the 30-year-old, however, as he said Ruiz would need "time to regain fitness" after spending three months on the sidelines."Fabian Ruiz needs more matches and minutes to recover," Luis Enrique insisted, before adding he was nonetheless "happy" with his return against Lyon.The former Barcelona and Spain coach warned that even as PSG close in on a repeat of their double-winning season this term, he still demands "more" from all his charges.Exciting Senegalese 18-year-old Ibrahim Mbaye was not included in the squad for Sunday's defeat to Lyon, with Luis Enrique explaining: "Every minute you get to play for PSG must be special."I have no regrets about Mbaye, but you have to be ready. He was ready, but I expect much more from all the players."Victory in the French capital against Nantes on Wednesday would send PSG three points clear of surprise Ligue 1 title challengers Lens with five matches remaining in the campaign.ali/nf/dmc
